items.prompt: A student wants the slope of the tangent line to a curve at a point, using the difference quotient (f(x+h) - f(x))/h. Which quantity should the student compute to get that slope exactly? Pick one option and give your reason.
items.reference_answer: The derivative is the slope of the tangent line, defined as a limit of difference quotients. A limit is the value the quotient approaches as the input h approaches 0, so it gives the instantaneous rate of change rather than a secant slope. Final answer: The limit of the quotient as h approaches 0.

items.prompt: A classmate says limits matter only as a side topic in calculus and that the derivative could be defined without them. Which role do limits actually play in the definition of the derivative? Pick one option and give your reason.
items.reference_answer: The derivative is the instantaneous rate of change, the slope of the tangent line, and it is defined as a limit of difference quotients. Without the limit as the input difference approaches 0, only average slopes over intervals would exist. Final answer: They are the foundation of the derivative definition.
